title: PAG, SAG and TCFG: what the extra guidance costs
hook: Three ways to add guidance without a prompt. Two pay with a whole extra prediction each step, and the third with one SVD. Read from source, with our renders.

verified.claim: PAG replaces middle-block self-attention with returning v, makes one more prediction on the positive, and adds scale times the difference.
SAG sets disable_cfg1_optimization, records middle-block attention on the unconditional, blurs, and makes one more prediction.
TCFG makes no extra prediction. It takes an SVD of the two scores and keeps the top direction of the unconditional.
score_tangential_damping's port equals the real function on test tensors.
verified.ref: Our comparison on a CPU, v0.43.0

verified.claim: The prediction counts in the lab come from a stand-in model following each node's logic.
The paper replaces the self-attention map with an identity, and pairs PAG with CFG.
The render timings and figures are stored measurements from one seed.

unchecked: Timings are wall clock polled every 1.5 s, so small differences mean nothing. Only PAG's gap is larger than the polling step.
That core PAG has no effect on a Flux or SD3 transformer, and that core SAG fails there, comes from reading those models' code. We did not run either combination.
We tested the stand-in counting logic, not a live run counting real model calls.
We read SAG's abstract only, and core's implementation in full.
